subject: Art & Design
title: Print vs. Digital: Different Rules Apply
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Print vs. Digital: Different Rules Apply.

hook.text: A stunning poster design can fall apart on a phone screen. Print and digital play by different rules.

buildup.text: Print is fixed: set size, CMYK color, tactile paper. Digital is fluid: variable screens, RGB, interaction.

discovery.text: Print resolution: 300 DPI. Screen resolution: 72-96 PPI (but retina doubles that). A print file on web is bloated.

twist.text: Print designers control every pixel. Digital designers surrender control — the user's device decides rendering.

climax.text: The best modern designers are fluent in both. Understanding constraints makes better design everywhere.

punchline.text: Know the medium. Then design for it, not against it.

quiz.question: What is the standard resolution for print design?

details.summary: Print and digital design share principles but differ in important ways. Print uses CMYK color, fixed layouts, and physical materials. Digital uses RGB color, responsive layouts, and interactive elements.
details.whyItMatters: Designing for print as if it were digital — or vice versa — produces poor results. Understanding medium-specific constraints and opportunities is essential for producing professional work in both environments.
takeaways: Print uses CMYK color; digital uses RGB color
Print has fixed layouts; digital requires responsive design
User behavior differs fundamentally between mediums

faq.question: Why do colors look different in print vs. screen?
faq.answer: Screens emit light (RGB), producing vibrant, luminous colors. Print reflects light from ink on paper (CMYK), producing more muted results. Neon greens and bright blues that look electric on screen often appear dull in print. Designers must proof colors in both mediums to avoid surprises.

faq.question: What does a print designer need to know about digital?
faq.answer: Responsive layouts adapt to screen sizes rather than fixed page dimensions. Interactive states (hover, click, scroll) add a time dimension print lacks. Resolution works differently (pixels per inch vs. dots per inch). And digital designs are never truly finished — they're updated continuously.
